chosenApproach: Expand IMCI under-two-month and under-five integrated checks while keeping formal classification and treatment for licensed clinicians. Add separate AJA 2.0 ages 10–19 consent-first, local-only, collapsible guide with emergency danger escalation and ad/AI blocking; mirror the standalone PWA guides.
selectionRationale: The existing English-only six-step IMCI description was static and failed to guide caregivers, while AI consultation and professional enrollment remain backend-gated. A small in-app local-first flow is useful without inventing clinician services or persisting sensitive data.
alternativeApproaches: Auto-classify IMCI disease or prescribe treatments: rejected because clinician assessment and currently adopted Philippine chart validation are required.
Store child symptoms in Supabase: rejected because no clinical purpose, consent, permissions or private health record backend is certified.
Activate AI/doctor portal flags prematurely: rejected until separate authenticated backend and health-professional verification.
